newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Thomson upgrades Lithuania, banks' ratings.
newsitem.headline: Thomson upgrades Lithuania, banks' ratings.

text.p: Rating agency Thomson Bankwatch on Wednesday said it has raised its sovereign rating for Lithuania and its senior debt rating for two leading banks Vilniaus Bankas and Hermis Bankas to BB from BB-.
The upgrades came after Standard & Poor's yesterday gave Lithuania a BBB minus for its long-term foreign currency debt and a BBB plus for its long-term local currency debt.

Thomson cited improved economic performance from stabilisation policies on the country rating and the continued leading position of Vilniaus and Hermis for their upgrades. "Not only has economic activity accelerated in recent years but inflation has fallen dramatically, down to 13.1 percent at the end of last year, marking its lowest level since independence," Thomson director of sovereign risk Betty Starkey said in a statement.
She said interest rates had fallen and that the currency board has kept the litas currency stable.

"The government has pursued a relatively cautious fiscal policy, which has led to substantial expenditure reductions," she added. She said that further efforts were needed to bolster fiscal finances but that progress to date has been noteworthy.

The agency also noted that Lithuania was boosting exports to the West, away from the former Soviet Union. The reorientation in trade along with the stabilisation efforts meant that GDP was forecast to grow by three and four percent this year.
Starkey said that Lithuania was politically the most stable of the three Baltic states and that the current government had a majority, which should allow it to continue reforms.
"Acceleration of these efforts will be critical to sustaining the country's economic recovery," Starkey added.
On the banks, the agency said that Vilniaus Bankas continued to be market leader while Hermis maintained an overall satisfactory financial condition.
"These upgrades denote our belief that both banks will continue to develop and remain the major commercial banks in the market," the agency added.
